honors.title: QUEST Best Capstone
honors.description:
Worked on a multi-disciplinary four person team in tandem with Northrop management to investigate optimization opportunities in Northrop Grumman's inventory management systems and processes. Recommendations sought to improve the overall inventory throughput rate by 10% and increase company production capacity annually by many hours, measured in several hundred thousand dollars, through a three part approach. 

Presentations were judged based on the impact and feasibility of the recommendations, the depth of analysis conducted, and the engagement of the final presentation. 

Personal contributions to the project included collaboration, consistent ideation, idealized thinking, data analysis, graphic design, presentation deck building, and public speaking. Deliverables include written reports, pitch decks, prototypes, and data analyses documents.
honors.issuer: Issued by QUEST Honors Program · Dec 2018

honors.title: Stamps Banneker Key Scholar
honors.description:
An academic four year full-ride scholarship and a stipend of $5000 awarded to four incoming freshmen.

The Stamps Banneker/Key Scholars join a select group of approximately 400 students from across the nation supported by the Stamps Family Charitable Foundation and are also part of the Stamps Banneker/Key Scholarship Program at University of Maryland.

Each of these students has been awarded a full merit scholarship that covers the entire cost of tuition, room, board, and a book allowance each year for four years of undergraduate study. The Stamps Banneker/Key Scholarship also provides up to $5000 per student to be used for research opportunities, internship experiences, travel to  professional meetings to present, study abroad, or other student-initiated learning opportunities approved on a case-by-case basis.

https://www.stampsscholars.org/our-program/
http://www.bannekerkey.umd.edu/ 
- The university partnership with the Stamps foundation was discontinued in 2018, which committed to sponsoring the existing scholars until graduation
honors.issuer: Issued by University of Maryland · Apr 2015

volunteerExperiences.description: Tzu Ching, the collegiate branch of Tzu Chi, is an international humanitarian organization and a non-governmental organization (NGO) with an international network of volunteers and employees. The branch at the University of Maryland serves the local DC metro area with a comprehensive set of outreach programs to local elementary schools, homeless shelters, retirement homes, food and clothes drives and more. On campus, the organization serves to share humanitarian values with the university community.
